clue.text: One with no funds — I'm aged, bottom in certain classifications

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
N.F. is the banking abbreviation for no funds, written on a bounced cheque
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
ae. abbreviates Latin aetatis, of the age of

explanation.surface: A penniless pensioner laments sitting at the bottom of the social classes.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'One with no funds' look like the subject of the sentence; it is just three abbreviations in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic an infima species is the lowest class in a scheme of classification; INFIMAE is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Striking deed of troublemaker before performance

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil
an act is a performance on stage

explanation.surface: A naughty child's showy stunt comes ahead of the main performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the collision of one body hitting another, so a blow or striking event.

clue.text: What land may be having story about member?

indicators.note: about means around, so the story is wrapped round the member

blocks.note: a fable is a moral tale
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what a piece of land might be if it features in a tale about some club member.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that can be cultivated or worked as a farm is said to be farmable.

clue.text: One wanting silence, restricting a person praying out loud

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the silence word closes around the article

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
mum, as in 'mum's the word', means silence
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wanting quiet keeps shushing a worshipper who prays aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: IMAUM is an old variant spelling of imam; the A sits inside MUM after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads congregational prayer in a mosque, reciting the prayers aloud for the worshippers.

clue.text: Dull subject — not one of education's essentials

indicators.note: the three essentials of schooling are the three Rs, and 'not one' says drop one of them

blocks.note: subject matter: the matter of a talk is its subject
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of education

explanation.surface: A boring school subject that fails to cover the basics of education.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove a single R from the end of MATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A matte finish is flat and without shine, so it looks dull rather than glossy.

clue.text: Dissolute star in time becomes favoured no longer

indicators.note: dissolute means loose and disordered in conduct, so these letters are broken up and loosened
the jumbled letters are placed inside the time word

blocks.note: an age is a period of time
the letters of star rearranged

explanation.surface: A debauched celebrity finds that, over time, fame and favour slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: AGRASTE is Spenser's past tense of aggrace, to show favour to; 'no longer' flags the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser used agraste to mean favoured or graced, a form now obsolete, which 'no longer' signals.

clue.text: Condescend, being old-style European going round India

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so the European surrounds the letter

blocks.note: a Dane, a native of Denmark, here with a nod to the Danish invaders of old
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to patronise others, behaving like a traditional European touring India.
explanation.walkthrough: DAINE is an archaic spelling of deign, which is why 'old-style' is there.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something beneath one's dignity, which is to condescend.

clue.text: Duke, last one to make a colourful contribution

definitions.text: one to make a colourful contribution

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
yester is an old word for last or previous, as in yesteryear

explanation.surface: The final contributor to a colourful project is a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like it means final in the list; here it means previous, as YESTER does.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyester is an old word for a dyer, a tradesman who adds colour to cloth.

clue.text: See a source of disease that flies around

indicators.note: turned around, the words are read from the far end back

blocks.note: sede is the Latin-derived word for a bishop's see or seat, as in sede vacante
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look at a disease carrier buzzing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look; it is a bishop's see, rendered SEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aedes is the genus of mosquito that carries yellow fever, dengue and Zika, a flying disease vector.

clue.text: Crazy romantics showing the influence of drugs?

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the following letters are set out in a mad new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Wild-eyed romantics look as though they are on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotism is the state of stupor induced by narcotic substances, that is, being under their effect.

clue.text: Opinionated leader of enterprise with ridiculous tenet

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
something ridiculous is absurdly wrong, so the following letters are set out absurdly

blocks.note: the opening letter of enterprise
the letters of tenet rearranged

explanation.surface: A company boss stubbornly clings to an absurd principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Entêté is a French borrowing meaning obstinate or headstrong, someone wedded to their own views.

clue.text: WI teased the old woman escort in the auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: the old woman is slang for one's mother, mama
to guide is to escort; guyed, meaning mocked, sounds the same

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute member ribbed an elderly woman's escort during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: WI looks like the Women's Institute, a British village club for women; here it is the West Indies, where mamaguy is Trinidadian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Trinidad and Tobago, to mamaguy someone is to tease, flatter or make fun of them.

clue.text: Clever expression, not half an attempt to show social division

indicators.note: not half says the word is cut short, losing its ending

blocks.note: a turn of phrase is a neat expression
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A smart remark, only half delivered, is a feeble attempt at showing class divisions.
explanation.walkthrough: PHRASE loses its last two letters, SE, rather than a strict half.
explanation.definitionFit: A phratry was a kinship group within an ancient Greek tribe; anthropologists use it for a grouping of clans.

clue.text: Sulk in Lochgilphead or Troon?

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of place names that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of Lochgilphead, the word or and the start of Troon

explanation.surface: A question whether someone is sulking in one Scottish town or another.
explanation.walkthrough: Lochgilphead and Troon are Scottish towns, which hints that the answer is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dort is Scots for to sulk, and in the plural, the dorts, a fit of the sulks.

clue.text: Grey matter is protected by this underwear packed for travel?

definitions.text: Grey matter is protected by this

blocks.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
something packed for travel is in a case, a suitcase

explanation.surface: Packing tip: keep your brain safe by wrapping it in underwear in the suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: The braincase is the cranium, the part of the skull enclosing and protecting the brain.

clue.text: Want a bishop (without being Italian) to lead church

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the Italian letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the chess notation for bishop
Sein is the philosophers' term, from German, for being

CE is the Church of England

explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads like a note on the bishop's nationality; it removes I from SEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Want can mean lack, as in 'for want of', and an absence is a lack of something.

clue.text: Colour of blood is awfully scary, enthralling yours truly

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters of the next word are badly arranged
to enthral is to hold captive, so the jumbled letters hold the setter inside

blocks.note: the letters of scary rearranged
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Blood red is frighteningly scary, and it captivates the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cramesy is an old spelling of cramoisy, crimson cloth or its deep red hue, the shade of blood.

clue.text: A certain ground having a sort of ridge

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A particular piece of ground has some kind of ridge across it.
explanation.definitionFit: Carinate means keeled, bearing a carina, the keel-like ridge on a bird's breastbone or a petal.

clue.text: By the end of street is bleak slab with inscription?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of street
the bleak is a small river fish, also called the ablet

explanation.surface: At the end of the street stands a grim stone slab with writing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bleak' reads as an adjective, grim; here it is the noun, a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a flat stone slab bearing a carved inscription, such as a memorial plaque.

clue.text: English writer to draw in a particular geometrical fashion

definitions.text: to draw in a particular geometrical fashion

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English

clue.text: Conservative out of a job? Express sympathy

on the dole is British for drawing unemployment benefit

clue.text: Pick up drug long delayed

blocks.note: E is ecstasy
something late has been held up a long time

explanation.surface: Collecting a drug order that has been held up for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To elate is to lift someone's spirits, to buck them up.

clue.text: Hair — the last thing you will want in beer

indicators.note: the last thing of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: Pils is a pilsner lager
the final letter of you

clue.text: Note Italian river, mostly calm

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

clue.text: Books with many a prayer or song?

blocks.note: taken as written
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the wordplay, so 'prayer' looks to pair with 'song'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oraria is a plural of orarium, a book of prayers or devotional manual.

clue.text: Transfer to another — an act getting reported

clue.text: Wind around part of hospital with one very good person

clue.text: I abandoned small room offered by landlord?
